html:
A confederation of Wolof states in what is now Senegal, founded about the mid-14th century, which tradition says was united by the legendary ruler Ndiadiane Ndiaye.

Its king, the Burba Jolof, received tribute from the kingdoms of Walo, Cayor and Baol and from the Serer states of Sine and Saloum. Portuguese ships arriving in the 1440s traded horses for captives along its coast, which strengthened the coastal kingdoms. In 1549 Cayor broke away after the battle of Danki, and the empire split into separate kingdoms that lasted until French conquest. Wolof became the common language of Senegal, spoken by most of its people. See also Mali and Lat Dior.
sum: A confederation of Wolof states in what is now Senegal, founded about the mid-14th century, which tradition says was united by the legendary ruler Ndiadiane Ndiaye.
